title: How to turn product photos into videos with AI
summary: Learn how to turn product photos into videos with AI, choose the right source images, templates, prompts, and formats, and create variations for every channel.
body_markdown:
You already have photos of the products you sell. They're on your website, in your marketplace listings, or ready for your next social media post. But what if those same images could become videos that show your products in action, introduce a new collection, or promote your next sale?


AI makes that possible without organizing a video shoot, hiring actors, or learning complicated editing software.


With[Photoroom](https://www.photoroom.com/) , you can turn existing product photos into short videos in two ways.[Video Ad Maker](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/ad-maker) creates complete promotional videos, with an AI director that helps you choose a creative approach, develop a script, and plan the scenes.[Product Animator](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/templates) lets you animate product images using ready-made motion templates or your own creative directions.


You don't need video production experience for either workflow. And you don't need to start from scratch every time you want to promote something new.


This guide walks you through both approaches, how to prepare your photos, which video styles work for different products, and how to create variations for your website, social media, marketplaces, and advertising campaigns.


## Can you turn product photos into videos with AI?


Yes. AI image-to-video tools can transform one or more static product photos into short videos by generating movement, changing the scene, introducing a presenter, or building a video around the product.


What you can create depends on the tool and the result you're looking for.


For example, you could turn a handbag photo into a short video showing the product from different angles. You could create a creator-led ad introducing a new skincare product, or make a promotional video for a seasonal collection using images you already have.


You don't necessarily need original video footage. Your existing product photos can provide the visual starting point.

## Why turn your existing product photos into videos?


Creating videos isn't just about making your product images move but giving customers another way to discover, understand, and evaluate what you're selling.


And for businesses that already have a collection of product images, AI video generation makes it possible to create more promotional content without organizing a new shoot for every campaign.


### Show more of your product


A static image captures one moment or angle. Video gives you room to show movement, highlight a detail, or introduce the product in a different setting.


For example, a short product video might focus on the texture of a skincare product, the silhouette of a handbag, or the way a piece of jewelry looks when worn.


You don't always need a long demonstration. Even a few seconds of focused video can help draw attention to a feature that might be overlooked in a static image.


### Create ads without filming


If you sell products online, you may need new promotional content for a launch, an upcoming sale, or a social media campaign.


Traditionally, that could mean planning a shoot, filming footage, editing clips, and preparing different versions for each channel.


AI video creation lets you start with the product photos you already have.


With Photoroom's Video Ad Maker, you can go further than animating an image: describe the ad you want, or let the AI director help plan the concept, script, scenes, and voice-over.


### Test different ways to promote the same product


You don't need a different product or a new photoshoot every time you want to experiment with advertising.


The same product images can support several creative approaches.


You might try a product-focused video, a creator-led introduction, or a promotional message built around a particular benefit. You can then compare how those approaches perform with your audience.


The goal isn't simply to make more videos. It's to give yourself more opportunities to find which messages and formats work for your products.


### Adapt videos for different markets and campaigns


A product launch, a holiday promotion, and a campaign targeting another country may all need different creative messages.


Instead of rebuilding everything from scratch, you can reuse your product images and adapt the style, script, language, or video format.


[Photoroom's Video Ad Maker](https://app.photoroom.com/video-ad-maker) supports multilingual voice-overs, making it possible to create versions for different audiences without recording new footage.


## How to choose the best product photos for AI videos


The quality of your starting images matters. AI can generate new scenes and movement, but it still needs clear references to understand what your product looks like.


Before creating your video, review the photos you're planning to use.


What to check


Why it matters


**Product visibility**


Make sure the product is clearly visible and isn't unnecessarily hidden by other objects


**Sharp details**


Labels, patterns, textures, and edges should be easy to identify


**Accurate colors**


Use images that represent the product you actually sell


**Multiple angles**


Different views can help communicate the product's shape and important details


**Consistent product variant**


Avoid mixing images showing different colors, sizes, or versions unless that's intentional


**Clean composition**


Keep distracting backgrounds or unnecessary objects from competing with the product


You don't need studio-perfect photography, and your images don't necessarily need white backgrounds.


A clean product photo works well when you want the item itself to be the focus. A lifestyle image can be useful when the setting helps communicate how or where the product is used.


### Prepare your product images before generating a video


If your source photos need improvement, it's worth fixing them before generating.


With Photoroom, you can use the[Background Remover](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/background-remover) to remove distracting backgrounds,[Product Staging](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/product-staging) to create lifestyle settings, or other[AI photo editing tools](https://www.photoroom.com/tools) to improve the presentation.


For example, imagine you sell handmade candles. You might start with a straightforward product photo for your listing, then create a lifestyle version showing the candle on a coffee table.


Both images can become useful starting points for different videos.


The benefit of preparing and generating content in the same workspace is that you don't have to move your product assets between separate editing and video tools.


## How to turn product photos into video ads with Photoroom


If you want to create a video that promotes a product, introduces a new collection, or supports an advertising campaign, start with[Photoroom's Video Ad Maker](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/ad-maker) .


It's designed to help sellers create video ads without complicated tools, prompt engineering, or traditional video editing.


You can describe what you want to achieve in simple, everyday language or let the AI director guide you through the creative process from the beginning.


Here's how it works.


### Step 1: Choose the product you want to promote


Start with a product that has a clear promotional purpose.


It could be a bestseller you want to advertise, a new arrival you're introducing, or an item you're including in a seasonal campaign.


Choose several clear photos showing the product from different angles. Include images showing important details or the product in use when you have them.


Open Video Ad Maker in Photoroom and add your images. You can upload photos, import them from Shopify, Google Drive, or Dropbox, or reuse designs you've already created in Photoroom.


The tool supports up to six product photos.


### Step 2: Tell the AI director what you want to create


You have two ways to start.


If you already have an idea, describe it in your own words. You don't need a technical prompt or detailed video production instructions.


For example:


-


"Create a short ad for my new skincare product that focuses on the packaging and texture."


-


"I want a creator-style video introducing this handbag."


-


"Make a promotional video for my holiday collection with an elegant, festive feel."


If you're not sure what kind of video would suit your product, let Photoroom's AI director take the lead instead.


In either case, the AI director asks a few questions to understand your goals and preferences. It can recommend a suitable video type, script, and format based on what you're selling and what you want to communicate.


You can follow its guidance or make your own creative choices.


### Step 3: Choose your video style


Photoroom offers a wide range of creative styles, so you're not limited to simply adding movement to a product photo.


Depending on your product and message, you might create a product showcase, a UGC-style ad, a product review, a before-and-after video, a creator-led story, or another custom concept.


For example, a jewelry seller might choose a product-focused video to highlight the design of a necklace. A beauty brand might prefer a creator-style ad introducing a product benefit.


You can accept the AI director's recommended approach, browse other available styles, or describe a custom idea.


You can also customize settings such as video length, format, language, audio, and AI actor, or leave relevant settings on Auto.


### Step 4: Review and customize the video plan


Before generating your video, Photoroom prepares a creative plan showing how the ad will unfold.


This includes the scenes, a shot-by-shot breakdown, the script, and the proposed voice-over.


You can review the plan and make changes before committing to the generation.


Pay particular attention to the product benefits and claims in the script. If the ad mentions something about your product, make sure it's accurate and you can substantiate it.


You can also adjust the creative direction if the suggested scenes, tone, or message don't match what you want.


This step is useful because you don't have to generate an entire video just to discover that the message isn't right.


### Step 5: Generate, review, and download your ad


Once you're happy with the creative plan, generate your video.


Photoroom's Video Ad Maker creates short ads of 5, 8, or 10 seconds, with vertical 9:16 and horizontal 16:9 options for different placements.


Review the finished video before publishing. Check that the product appearance, colors, packaging, logos, and details are represented accurately.


When you're satisfied, download the video and use it on your website, social media, or supported advertising platforms.


You can also create additional versions with different messages, creative styles, or languages.


For example, you might test a product showcase against a creator-led ad, then prepare a new version for an upcoming seasonal campaign.


## How to animate a product photo with AI


Not every product video needs a script, an actor, or an advertising concept.


Sometimes you simply want to bring a static image to life: add a slow camera movement, create a product reveal, or show the item from a more dynamic angle.


That's where[Photoroom's Product Animator](https://www.photoroom.com/tools/video-generator/templates) comes in.


Unlike Video Ad Maker, which builds a complete promotional video, Product Animator gives you control over an individual visual concept and the way your product moves within it.


### Step 1: Upload your product photo


Open Product Animator and add the image you want to animate.


A single clear image can work well for simple effects, such as a gentle camera movement or product reveal.


If your product has important details on multiple sides, additional reference images may help the generator understand its shape and appearance.


### Step 2: Choose a template or describe the effect


Photoroom provides more than 300 e‑commerce video templates, covering different product categories, camera movements, and visual effects.


You can choose a ready-made template or describe your own concept.


For example, you might want a slow camera movement around a handbag, a close-up that emphasizes the texture of a skincare bottle, or a product reveal with soft studio lighting.


Templates are useful when you want a clear starting point without planning the movement yourself. Custom instructions give you more control when you have something specific in mind.


### Step 3: Set the scene and format


Depending on the workflow you choose, you can adjust the background, mood, framing, camera movement, and product action.


Choose the aspect ratio based on where you plan to use the finished video.


A vertical video may be suitable for Reels, Stories, or mobile-first advertising, while a horizontal format can work for wider website placements and other video channels.


The tool also supports square output for relevant placements.


### Step 4: Review the first frame and generate


Preview and adjust the first frame before generating the full video.


Use this opportunity to check that the product, setting, and composition look right.


If something is wrong, adjust the image, template, or creative instructions before continuing.


Once you're satisfied, generate the video and review the result.


Check that the product remains visually consistent and that the chosen movement doesn't distort important features.


You can then export the finished video as an MP4.


## Which AI product video style should you choose?


The most useful video style depends on the product you're selling and what you want people to notice.


Here are a few examples.


Video style


When it makes sense


Example


**Product showcase**


When the item itself should be the focus


Highlighting the design and details of a handbag


**UGC-style ad**


When you want a creator-like presentation or introduction


An AI presenter introducing a new skincare product


**Product review or explainer**


When a product needs a short spoken explanation


Introducing the benefits of a kitchen gadget


**Before-and-after video**


When a supported transformation is central to the product story


Demonstrating a legitimate, verifiable product result


**Lifestyle video**


When context helps customers picture the product in use


Showing home accessories in a furnished room


**Product animation**


When you want controlled motion without a full advertising concept


A slow rotation or camera movement around a shoe


**Seasonal promotional video**


When a campaign needs a specific theme or message


Promoting a holiday gift collection


These styles aren't tied exclusively to one selling channel.


A product showcase might work on your website and in a social post. A creator-led video might be useful in a paid campaign, while a simple product animation could complement a marketplace listing that supports video.


The important thing is to choose a style that makes sense for your product and the message you want to communicate, rather than adding effects just because they're available.


## How to create product video variations without starting over


Once you've created one product video, you don't have to treat it as a one-off asset.


You can use the same product photos to develop other creative approaches for launches, promotions, and different audiences.


### Test different messages


Imagine you're selling a reusable water bottle.


One ad might focus on its design, another on its practical features, and a third on its suitability for everyday travel.


You can create variations around those messages and compare their performance.


For a meaningful test, try to change one main creative element at a time. That makes it easier to understand what might be influencing the results.


### Adapt your videos for seasonal campaigns


You might promote the same product differently during a summer sale, a holiday gifting campaign, or a new collection launch.


Instead of organizing new photography for each occasion, reuse your existing product images and update the creative direction, setting, or promotional message.


This gives you flexibility to respond to new opportunities without rebuilding your visual content from the beginning.


### Create versions for different countries and languages


If you sell internationally, you may want to communicate with customers in their own language.


**Photoroom's Video Ad Maker supports multilingual AI voice-overs, helping you create localized versions of your ads using the same product assets.**


Remember that localization goes beyond translating the script. Review product terminology, cultural references, promotional claims, and any market-specific offers before publishing.


### Adapt videos for different placements


A video that works on your product page might need a different format or creative opening for a social media ad.


Always check the requirements of the destination platform before publishing, especially for marketplaces and[paid advertising](https://www.photoroom.com/blog/ecommerce-video-ads) .


For Video Ad Maker, Photoroom supports 9:16 and 16:9 formats. Product Animator also offers other aspect ratios for appropriate use cases.
